[[Barclays Center Classic]] champions |tourney = [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = round of 32 }} {{2014–15 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2014–15 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], in their 110th season of play. The team was led by head coach Tony Bennett, in his sixth year, and played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. Building on the success of [[2013–14 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|the previous season]], the Cavaliers had their best regular season in program history with a record of 28–2, their first undefeated non-conference regular season record since [[2000–01 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2000–01]], and their highest national ranking since [[1982–83 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|1982–83]], ranking at number two on the AP Poll for a total of seven weeks. The Cavaliers also became the first team outside of [[Tobacco Road rivalry|Tobacco Road]] to win back-to-back ACC regular season championships, with their conference record of 16–2. Particular highlights included holding Rutgers, Harvard, and Georgia Tech to under thirty points each. Virginia also held Harvard to a single field goal in the first half of their game, tying the NCAA record for fewest field goals allowed in the first half of a game since the [[shot clock]] was instituted in 1986.{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/no-virginia-hammers-harvard-in-historic-fashion/article_9f233f4a-8944-11e4-b194-8be8c6067517.html |title=No. 6 Virginia hammers Harvard in historic fashion |first=Whitey |last=Reid |work=[[The Daily Progress]] |date=22 December 2014 |accessdate=22 December 2014}}{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/101636/the-most-impressive-part-of-uvas-49-point-win |title=Most impressive part of UVa's 49-point win |first=Eammonn |last=Brennan |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=22 December 2014 |access-date=22 December 2014}} However, late-season injuries, in particular [[Justin Anderson (basketball)|Justin Anderson's]] nearly five-week-long absence due to a broken finger and appendectomy, hurt the team, with the Cavaliers falling in a close loss to North Carolina in the [[2015 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] semifinals. In the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] they defeated Belmont in the second round before losing in the third round to Michigan State. ==Last season== The [[2013–14 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Cavaliers]] finished the season 30–4 overall and 16–2 in conference play, finishing in first place in the ACC outright for the first time since [[1980–81 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|the 1980–81 season]]. They proceeded to win the [[2014 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] for their second-ever conference championship. The team also tied for the most wins in a season in school history, set a school record for the most single-season conference wins, and earned their highest final national ranking since [[1981–82 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|1982]]. The Cavaliers received a #1 seed in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they defeated [[2013–14 Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball team|Coastal Carolina]] and [[2013–14 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]] before losing to [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the Sweet Sixteen.{{cite web | title = Curtain Falls on Extraordinary Basketball Season | url = http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032914aac.html | website= VirginiaSports.com - The University of Virginia Official Athletic Site | date = 29 March 2014 | accessdate = 8 August 2014}} ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
